input.command: for n in 117 118 114; do echo "=========== #$n ==========="; gh issue view $n --json title,body --jq '.title, .body' | head -45; done
input.description: Read the three restore_curline issues

result.output:
=========== #117 ===========
A resize does not restore an ended prompt once the answer is part typed
#112 restores a prompt that ended its own line — `prout` appends the newline, so
`curline` is empty by the time the reader waits, and the question used to vanish
on a resize. The fix keeps the finished line and puts it back.

It deliberately does **not** do so once the player has begun typing.

## Why

An ended prompt and its part-typed answer occupy two rows, with curses' padding
between them. `restore_curline()` compares against a single joined string, and
spanning that boundary went wrong twice in review:

- Leaving the answer out of the comparison meant the tail test never fired, so a
  drag reprinted the question **once per width step** — copies stacking up the
  window, which is the exact failure `restore_curline()`'s comparison exists to
  prevent.
- Padding the answer back to the row boundary fixed that and turned a one-row
  height shrink (80x24 → 80x23) into a **second copy** instead.

Both were found by `ui-review`; the second was my fix for the first.

## What happens now

With an answer part typed, an ended prompt is left alone on a resize — the
behaviour before #112. The answer itself is still restored by the ordinary
`curline` path, so the player can see what they have typed; the question above
it is at worst truncated, exactly as it was.

That is milder than either failure above, which is why it is the state that
ships. It is still worth fixing.

## Fix sketch

The comparison needs to model two rows rather than one. Either:

- build `want` as prompt, padding, answer and verify it against what
  `mvwinnstr()` actually returns for the prompt row — the padding assumption is
  what broke on the height shrink, and it should be measured rather than
  computed; or
- compare the two parts separately, locating the prompt row first and the answer
  row under it, which avoids the padding question entirely.

The rewrite branch needs the same care: `rows` currently adds the prompt and
answer lengths together, and for an ended line they do not share a row.
=========== #118 ===========
A height shrink can let a restored ended prompt overwrite live conversation
`restore_curline()`'s erase branch assumes the rows at the bottom of the message
window are the stump of the line it is restoring. Where a height shrink clipped
an ended prompt away instead, they are not, and the reprint lands on real
conversation.

## How to see it

```
./build/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw
rest 5000   -> "Are you sure?"   answer n
rest 5000   -> "Are you sure?"   answer n
rest 5000   -> "Are you sure?"   leave it pending
resize 80x24 -> 78x20
```

Gives:

```
 COMMAND> rest 5000
 Are you sure?
 Are you sure?
```

The `n` that answered the middle ask has been overwritten by the restored
question, so the transcript reads as though the game asked twice in a row.

## Scope

Not a regression, and better than what it replaces. `main` at the same shape
shows the last line as `n` with no question at all and the reader silently
waiting — which is #112 itself. So this is a net improvement that leaves a
smaller artifact behind.

## Fix sketch

The branch computes how many rows the stump occupies from the old width and
erases back from the last non-blank row. That is right when the bottom rows
really are the stump. Where the shrink discarded the prompt rather than
truncating it, the rows it erases are older conversation.

Distinguishing them needs something the branch does not currently have: whether
the line being restored was on screen at all before the resize. The search
above already answers that — it fell through, which is why the branch was

restore_curline()'s height-only branch anchors to the bottom of the window
`restore_curline()` in `tui.c` has two branches for placing the line it rebuilds.

The `oldmsgw > 0` branch — the terminal's width changed — anchors to the last row
with anything on it, and its comment explains why that matters:

> Anchored to the last row with anything on it, not to the bottom of the window.
> They are the same once the conversation has filled it, and different for the
> whole setup conversation and after every `clearscreen()` -- there the live line
> sits mid-window, and writing at the bottom left the stump above it with blank
> rows in between.

The `else` branch — width unchanged, so only the height moved — does not:

```c
wscrl(wmsg, 1);
wmove(wmsg, maxy - 1, 0);
```

The same argument applies to it. Where the conversation has not filled the
window, this puts the rebuilt line at the bottom with blank rows above it,
instead of directly under the conversation.

## Why it is not fixed already

It cannot be reached to be tested. Getting into that branch needs the pending
pair — the game's part-written line plus the answer being typed — to be longer
than the whole message window, since a pair that fits is found intact by the
search above and the branch is never entered. The longest pair the game can
produce is a prompt plus the 126-character input buffer, about 135 characters.
The smallest message window with two rows to scroll is wider than that.

So the defect is real by inspection and unreachable by construction, at least at
every terminal size the display accepts.

A fix would be the same expression the other branch uses, but it interacts with
the `wscrl()` on the line above — after a scroll the row that `last` named holds
different content — so it is not a copy-paste, and there is no way to observe
whether it is right.

## What would make it testable

Either a larger input buffer (`tui.c`'s own comment at the top of
`restore_curline()` says the 512/2048 buffers there want revisiting if the input
buffer grows), or a message window smaller than two rows of the longest pair,

		   an answer the two sit on separate rows with curses'
		   padding between them, and every attempt at spanning that
		   went wrong in a different way: dropping the answer from
		   the comparison reprinted the question once per drag step,
		   and padding it back turned a one-row height shrink into a
		   second copy. What is left unfixed is milder than either
		   -- what is left is exactly what the game did before this
		   change, which at some shapes is a blank message window
		   with the reader still waiting. Worse than restoring it
		   would be; better than restoring it twice. Issue #117. */
		if (pending_answer != NULL && *pending_answer != '\\0')
			return;
		line = lastline;"""
b1 = """		line = lastline;"""
assert t.count(a1) == 1, "gate"
t = t.replace(a1, b1)

# 2. want: the question alone for an ended line
a2 = """	/* An ended line puts the answer on the row below, and curses pads
	   the rest of the prompt's row with blanks to get there. Those
	   blanks are in the joined rows, so they have to be in `want`
	   too: without them the answer never matched, the tail test
	   failed, and a drag reprinted the question at every step --
	   the same copies-up-the-window this comparison exists to stop,
	   reintroduced for the ended case. */
	i = ended && width > 0 && linelen % width != 0
	    ? width - linelen % width : 0;
	snprintf(want, sizeof want, "%s%*s%s", line, i, "",
		 pending_answer == NULL ? "" : pending_answer);
	wantlen = (int)strlen(want);"""
b2 = """	/* The pair shares a row only when the line did not end. An ended
	   one puts the answer on the row below, so on screen they are two
	   strings and not one, and joining them here is what both failed
	   attempts at this did: leaving the answer out made the tail test
	   fail against an answer that was there, and padding it to the
	   row boundary made it fail against one that was not. Neither can
	   be right, because a height shrink cuts the answer's row and
	   keeps the question's -- so what is on screen is half of what
	   was written, and a single string can only match all or none of
	   it. Look for the question, and let the tail test below account
	   for the answer separately. */
	snprintf(want, sizeof want, "%s%s", line,
		 ended || pending_answer == NULL ? "" : pending_answer);
	wantlen = (int)strlen(want);"""
assert t.count(a2) == 1, "want"

**Why it matters to a player.** On a one-row height shrink (80x24 → 80x23) `wresize()` cuts the answer's row and keeps the question's, so the screen reads as a clean unanswered question while the reader still holds the typed `y`. I reproduced it: typing `N` there submits `yN`, `ja()` takes the `y`, `rest 5000` runs, and the game ends with "Your time has run out and the Federation has been conquered." At 80x14 and 20x8 the whole exchange disappears instead.

**The fix.** The comparison now models two rows rather than one, which is the second of the two options the issue's fix sketch offers:
- `want` is the question alone for an ended line, not question+padding+answer. A single joined string can only match all or none of the pair, and a height shrink leaves exactly half of it on screen.
- The read-back goes one row further for an ended line, since the answer has a row of its own and `wantlen` no longer counts it.
- The tail test steps over curses' padding to the end of the question's row and then over the answer, before asking whether the rest is blank. Either may be absent. Anything else found on the way is still reported as a real overwrite.

The write path already put an ended line's answer on the row below and set `cursor_at_prompt`, which makes `tui_readline()` re-echo the answer — none of that changed.

**What the fix deliberately does not do.** It restores the *display*. It does not discard the buffered `y`, so typing `N` after a resize still answers yes. That is the player's to clear and `sst.doc` tells them how; what the fix buys is that they can see there is something to clear. Verified: after the fix, `y` then 80x23 and back shows the question and the `y` under it, and Ctrl-U then `n` answers no and returns to `COMMAND>`.

**Test.** `tests/tui.sh`'s #117 block asserted only "never more than one question", which tolerated zero. It now asserts the question exactly once **and** the typed answer on the row below it. It failed at all three drag sizes before the change and passes at all three after; nothing else in that file moved.

when `curlen == 0` and a reader is waiting. Two different readers can be
waiting there, and only one of them is covered:

- `tui_getch()` does not, so `pending_answer` is NULL.

a `pause(1)`, and nothing in the suite reaches one.

The `verifier` mutated `tui.c` with

```c
if (pending_answer == NULL) return;
```

immediately after `ended = TRUE`, and the whole suite stayed green — 11/11 in
both configurations. That mutant disables the restore for exactly the
`tui_getch()` case.

## Why it matters

`pause(1)` is the announcement pause: `sst.c:770-776` writes
`[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]` or
`[IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING -- HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` with `prout`

and this is an ended line by construction — the same shape #112 was about. A
resize there with the restore broken leaves the player looking at a screen with
no prompt on it, waiting on a keystroke they have not been asked for.

the help pager, which is `proutn("[CONTINUE?]")` / `proutn("[HIT SPACE BAR TO

`pause(1)` is only called from `ai.c:354`, `:516` and `:565`, all of them

deterministically means driving the game to an event rather than issuing a

Review the current branch diff and every staged, unstaged and untracked file in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. The change is unstaged on `main` at `8fbb4db` (I have not branched yet — flag that if you think it matters, I will branch before committing). Four files: `tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `sst.doc`, `README.md`. It fixes issue #117 — read the issue and both of its comments, which carry measurements.

**The defect.** `restore_curline()` refused to restore a prompt that ended its own line once the player had begun typing an answer. The gate was deliberate: two earlier attempts at spanning the row boundary between an ended prompt and its answer each duplicated the question, one per width step in the first and once on a one-row height shrink in the second.

**Why it matters to a player.** On a one-row height shrink `wresize()` cuts the answer's row and keeps the question's, so the screen reads as a clean unanswered question while the reader still holds the typed `y`. I reproduced the whole thing: typing `N` there submits `yN`, `ja()` takes the `y`, `rest 5000` runs, and the game ends with "Your time has run out and the Federation has been conquered."

**The fix** — the second of the two options the issue's fix sketch offers, model two rows rather than one:
- `want` is the question alone for an ended line; a single joined string can only match all or none of the pair, and a height shrink leaves half of it on screen
- the read-back steps back over every row the answer takes
- the tail test steps over curses' padding and then over as much of the answer as is on screen — a prefix, since the shrink truncates it

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
cat > "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/i10.md" <<'EOF'
`restore_curline()`'s joined-row search reads each row with

```c
mvwinnstr(wmsg, rr, 0, onscreen, (int)sizeof onscreen - 1);
```

`onscreen` is 512 bytes, so it reads at most 511 columns. The search depends on
every appended row being *exactly* the window's width — that is what makes
`start`, `skip % width`, `bound` and `i / width` mean columns. Past 511 the rows
come back short, they stop lining up end to end, and the search misses a pair
that is perfectly intact.

The fix for #117 added a guard that returns rather than falling through, since
falling through stacks a copy of the question at every step of a drag. So at a
message window of 512 columns or more — a terminal of 514 — an ended prompt and
its part-typed answer are simply not restored.

## What a player sees

The same as before #117 at that width: on a height shrink the answer's row is
cut and the question's survives, so the screen reads as a clean unanswered
question while the reader still holds what was typed. `main` behaved the same
way, so this is not a regression — it is the one shape #117's fix does not
reach.

It is also why `sst.doc` and `README.md` say the line "usually" comes back
rather than that it does. The manual describes the short-window gap, which a
player can recognise on screen; it does not name a column count.

## How to see it

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L wide new-session -d -x 600 -y 24 './build/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw'
# rest 5000, type y without Enter, then resize to -y 23 and back
```

At 513 columns the pair restores. At 514 it does not. `tests/tui.sh` covers the
guard itself at 600 columns — that the question is not duplicated and a
keystroke does not land on it — but nothing asserts a restore there, because
there is none to assert.

## Fix sketch

Two routes, and the second is the better one.

- Size the buffers from the terminal rather than fixing them at 512/2048.
  `restore_curline()` would need `onscreen` at `COLS` and `joined` at roughly
  four times that, which means allocating rather than declaring — the function
  is called on every repaint, so a static buffer grown on demand would suit it
  better than malloc per call.
- Stop joining rows at all. The search only needs to find the question and then
  look at what follows it, and the ended case already treats the answer as a
  separate string; comparing row by row would remove both the width dependence
  and the `joined` buffer. That is close to the second option #117's own fix
  sketch offered, carried one step further.

## Provenance

Found by `code-review` while reviewing the fix for #117, which made the path
reachable — an ended line's answer always has a row of its own, so the ended
case always joins more than one row, where nothing else at that width spans
two. Filed rather than fixed there: the buffers are a separate decision from
the two-row model, and 514 columns is far outside anything the manual
describes.
EOF

You reviewed this three times. Round 3 returned "acceptable as-is" plus one should-fix and two nits, all documentation, all taken. **This round exists because `code-review` pointed out that two player-visible things have landed since you last looked**, and it was right to insist:

**1. A width guard in `restore_curline()` that did not exist when you last saw it.** Past 511 columns `mvwinnstr` reads a short row, the joined rows stop lining up end to end, and the search misses a pair that is perfectly intact — after which the write path stacks a copy of the question at every step of a drag. My change made that reachable, because an ended line's answer always has a row of its own so the ended path always joins more than one row. The guard returns instead of falling through. `code-review` reproduced the original failure at 600x24: the question alternating on and off with `yre you sure?` corruption stacked twice up the window.

**2. Its placement, which I got wrong first.** I put the guard after the row scan. `row_blank()` is `mvwinnstr`, which moves the cursor, so the return parked the player's next keystroke at column 0 of the question — a typed character landing on the question instead of after the answer. The `verifier` caught it. The guard now sits above the scan.

So at 512 columns and above, an ended prompt with a part-typed answer is **not restored** — the same as `main`, and filed as #136. That is the newest player-facing behaviour in the diff and no screen-reading pass has seen it.

**3. What I want, driven rather than read:

- whether the wide-terminal behaviour is acceptable to a player as it now stands, and whether the screen at 512+ columns is honest about what the game is holding
- whether the cursor lands where the next keystroke belongs at those widths, and whether anything a player types can go somewhere they would not expect
- whether the rewritten `sst.doc` and `README.md` passages are now true at **both** ends — the short window and the very wide one — and whether a player following them does the right thing at each
- whether anything at ordinary sizes has moved since round 3

content.text:
**#117 is closed.** `main` is at `58f5ea6`, all four CI jobs green, tree clean.

## The bug, and why it was worth doing first

On a one-row height shrink, `wresize()` cuts the answer's row and keeps the question's. The screen read as a **clean unanswered question** while the reader still held the typed `y`. I reproduced the whole thing: typing `N` submitted `yN`, `ja()` took the `y`, and the game ended with *"Your time has run out and the Federation has been conquered."*

The fix models two rows instead of one — the question alone in the comparison, a read-back that steps over every row the answer takes, and a tail test that accepts as much of the answer as survived the cut.

It restores the *display*, not the buffer: typing `N` after a resize still answers yes. That's the player's to clear, and the manual says how. What the fix buys is that they can see there's something to clear.

## What review caught that I didn't

- **`code-review` found a blocker at 600 columns.** Past 511, `mvwinnstr` reads a short row and the joined rows stop lining up — and my change is what made that reachable. My first guard for it was placed *after* the row scan, which moves the cursor, so it parked the next keystroke on the question. The `verifier` failed that placement.
- **`ui-review` found a wrapping answer stacking three copies** of the whole exchange on every height step — exactly the failure the old gate existed to prevent.
- **The manual I wrote earlier this session went false**, and was telling players to Ctrl-U and retype an answer that is now intact — the self-destruct password included.

Passes: `ui-review` ×4, `verifier` ×8, `code-review` ×4.

## On the tests

Every assertion was made to fail before I trusted it, and each proof is recorded beside it — including the one where my own claim was wrong. I wrote that no single edit could produce the opposite of the too-short state; the verifier found one (`maxy > 1` → `maxy > 2`), and I reproduced it. The comment now records that break instead of my excuse.

The `verifier` killed 8 mutants independently, including both historical failed attempts at this fix.

## Filed

**#134** (ended branch at a pause uncovered), **#135** (two exact-fill guards untested), **#136** (no restore past 513 columns). Commented on **#90**, **#94**, **#115**, **#122**, and on **#117** itself — twice, the second time correcting my own earlier comment, which claimed both halves are always lost when which half survives depends on what the resize clipped.

One thing I'd flag: **#135's two guards are introduced by this change**, so filing didn't discharge them — that's recorded as an explicit resolution, not a deferral. They only fire for a prompt whose length exactly divides the message window, and nothing in the game reaches that today. The thing to watch is a future 70-character prompt, not a terminal width.
